units.name: Ceuta
units.summary: Ceuta (autonomous city): state wealth tax rules (75% rebate only for assets located in Ceuta); inheritance 99% rebate when the deceased lived in Ceuta for 5 years; gifts 50%. Savings income (gains, dividends) is taxed on the national 19-30% scale; the regions cannot change it.

inheritance.summary: Ceuta: state rules with a 99% rebate for Groups I-II when the deceased was habitually resident in Ceuta or Melilla on death and for the previous 5 years (art. 23 bis Ley 29/1987); about 0.33% of a EUR 10m inheritance.
inheritance.exemptions_thresholds: State reduction EUR 15,956.87 and state scale; 99% rebate if the 5-year residence condition is met.
inheritance.important_exceptions: The 99% rebate requires the deceased's habitual residence in Ceuta or Melilla on death and for the previous 5 years; otherwise the state scale applies in full (the basic 50% rebate of art. 23 bis.1 also depends on that residence).

units.name: Comunidad Foral de Navarra
units.summary: Navarra (foral regime, own taxes): savings income taxed at 20-28%; own wealth tax from EUR 550,000 at 0.16%-2%, with a 3.5% band above EUR 11m base that replaces the state ITSGF; children's inheritances: first EUR 250,000 free, then 2%-16% (about 13.5% on EUR 10m); gifts 0.8%-8%. The state Beckham regime does not apply.

capital_gains.summary: Navarra has its own IRPF: gains and dividends are taxed on a savings scale of 20% to 28% (28% above EUR 300,000).
capital_gains.exemptions_thresholds: Navarra savings scale (art. 60 DFL 4/2008, wording of Ley Foral 36/2022 in force since 1 January 2023 and unchanged in the consolidated text for 2026): 20% to EUR 6,000; 22% to 10,000; 24% to 15,000; 26% to 200,000; 27% to 300,000; 28% above.
capital_gains.regional_differences: Applies to residents of Navarra under the Convenio Económico (residence by days in the tax year).
capital_gains.important_exceptions: Navarra has its own exit-tax rules and its own impatriate regime for displaced workers (Modelos 149/150 of Hacienda Foral; not modelled); the state Beckham regime does not apply.

wealth_tax.summary: Navarra: own wealth tax, EUR 550,000 allowance, 0.16%-2.0% and 3.5% above EUR 11.0m of base (in place of the ITSGF). Tax on EUR 5m: EUR 45,964; EUR 10m: EUR 128,280; EUR 20m: EUR 453,364.

units.name: País Vasco / Euskadi
units.summary: Basque Country (foral regime, three territories with own taxes; numbers modelled on Bizkaia): savings income 19-28%; wealth tax from EUR 800,000 at 0.2%-2%, foral ITSGF only at the top; children's inheritances: EUR 400,000 allowance then a flat 1.5% (Bizkaia and Gipuzkoa), gifts 1.5% from the first euro. Foral rules apply to arrivals from abroad at once, but not if the deceased/donee spent more of the last 5 years in common-regime Spain. The state Beckham regime does not apply.

capital_gains.summary: The Basque Country has its own IRPF per territory; from 1 January 2026 Álava, Bizkaia and Gipuzkoa apply the same savings scale, 19% to 28% (28% above EUR 300,000).
capital_gains.regional_differences: The three territories legislate separately, but NF 2/2025 (Bizkaia), NF 3/2025 (Álava) and NF 1/2025 (Gipuzkoa) adopted the same savings scale with effect from 1 January 2026 (Cuatrecasas, May 2025); Bizkaia's consolidated text was checked directly.
capital_gains.important_exceptions: Basque impatriate regime instead of the state Beckham regime.

wealth_tax.summary: Basque Country (modelled on Bizkaia): own wealth tax, EUR 800,000 allowance, 0.2%-2.0%; the foral solidarity tax (NF 9/2023, 800,000 allowance, 1.5%-3.5%) tops it up only at the very top (about EUR 16.8m of net wealth and above). Combined IP+ITSGF on net wealth (after the main-home exemption) of EUR 5m: EUR 37,400; EUR 10m: EUR 119,400; EUR 20m: EUR 358,500.
wealth_tax.exemptions_thresholds: Bizkaia: allowance EUR 800,000; main home exempt up to EUR 400,000; joint limit with IRPF 65% of the IRPF base, IP reduction capped at 75%.
wealth_tax.regional_differences: Bizkaia is modelled. Per Guía Fiscal (secondary source, updated 29/07/2026): Álava (NF 9/2013, revised by NF 3/2025) has the same EUR 800,000 allowance and EUR 400,000 main-home exemption but its own 8-band scale topping out at 2.5%; Gipuzkoa (NF 2/2018, revised by NF 1/2025) has a EUR 700,000 allowance, EUR 300,000 main-home exemption and a 2.5% top rate. Each territory has its own foral solidarity tax (Bizkaia NF 9/2023, Gipuzkoa NF 3/2023, Álava NF 23/2023) for net wealth above EUR 3m, credited against the foral IP. So Álava and Gipuzkoa are somewhat more expensive than the modelled Bizkaia figures at high wealth.
wealth_tax.important_exceptions: The ITSGF is a concerted tax with foral rules (Concierto DA 5ª); each territory adopted its own norm (Bizkaia NF 9/2023).
